label: Takeaway
detail: Indiana Tech went 43-17 overall and 24-4 in the WHAC, split two WHAC Tournament final games with Madonna on May 3, losing the title, and went 2-2 at the NAIA Opening Round in Upland. Its posted 2027 roster keeps 57% of 2026 plate appearances and 42% of innings, and adds 46 new names. Ferguson, Rainey and Hannah are on it. Ruiz, Morrison, Santana and Redmon are not.

label: Method
detail: Back means a 2026 player whose name is on Indiana Tech's posted 2027 roster. Everyone else who played counts as out, either as a listed senior or grad student or as not on the roster. A posted roster can still change before the season.

label: Season
detail: 43-17 followed 38-21 in 2025. McWilliams's bio calls it the most wins since 2018, and the schedule pages agree: 44 in 2018, 42 in 2019. Indiana Tech scored 546 runs and allowed 327, and finished second in the WHAC standings behind Northwestern Ohio at 25-3.

label: Postseason
detail: WHAC Tournament, Grand Rapids and Rockford, Apr 30-May 3: lost to Lawrence Tech 6-5, then beat Siena Heights 4-1, Cornerstone 18-9, Lawrence Tech 6-4, Cleary 13-2 and Madonna 10-9 before losing to Madonna 9-6. NAIA Opening Round, Upland, May 11-13, with an at-large bid: beat Abraham Baldwin 16-10 and Shawnee State 9-3, and lost to Taylor 19-5 and 22-10.

label: lu_proj
detail: Built from 2026 box scores, using only players on the posted 2027 roster with a 2026 Indiana Tech record. Order is by 2026 OPS, so small samples rank high. Ferguson, Dunkle, Hannah, Rainey and Richards each made at least 44 starts at that position. Seefeldt made 12 at first and Hammond 9 at DH. Nobody back made a start at second. Filandrinos, listed as an infielder for 2027, had 2 at-bats, and Laymon made 1 start in left. New names have no 2026 stats here, so none is in a projected spot.

label: lu_most
detail: A typical 2026 lineup, built from all 60 box scores. Each position goes to the player with the most starts there, using each player once and keeping as many of those starts as possible; the DH spot counts only starts at DH. The order is each player's average spot across all his 2026 starts, lowest first. 2027 outlook is the same status used on the rest of this page.

label: lu_all
detail: Indiana Tech used 40 different lineups in 60 games. A lineup counts as the same only with the same nine in the same order at the same positions.

label: rot_proj
detail: The same 2026 stats, with projected 2027 roles from the posted roster. Pitchers not on it made 35 of the 60 starts, including Redmon's 15, Myers's 11 and Byford's 9. Hammond and Baughman have 15 starts between them. New names have no 2026 stats here, so these are role guesses from 2026 usage.

label: Staff
detail: Main starters made at least 4 starts. Relievers made at least 5 relief outings and aren't main starters. GS and Relief are published totals.

label: Maps
detail: Each of the 11 players with a Michigan hometown is plotted here, out of 49 with a listed hometown. 22 list Indiana and show on the national map below, since Indiana Tech is in Fort Wayne. The hot zone is a density estimate over the Michigan towns, so color shows concentration, not exact locations.

label: League
detail: Indiana Tech ranked 1st of 11 WHAC teams in runs per game (9.10) and 1st in walk rate. On the mound it ranked 2nd in ERA (5.33) and 9th in homers allowed per nine (0.88). Its .967 fielding percentage ranked 2nd.

label: Method
detail: wOBA uses standard big-league weights. FIP uses a constant that sets the NAIA-wide FIP equal to NAIA ERA. Rank 1 is best in every row. Indiana Tech's numbers are from NAIA stats, which has all 60 games, and its WHAC rank is out of 11 teams because Rochester Christian isn't listed.

label: Filter
detail: All games shows Indiana Tech's published totals. Any other filter is added up from box scores and play-by-play, game by game. The filter changes the Hitters, Pitchers and Tendencies tabs. Player cards always show the full season.

label: Outing log
detail: Days of rest counts full calendar days since the pitcher's previous appearance, whatever the filter. Pitch counts show a dash when a box score lists none.

label: Jack Ferguson
detail: Ferguson hit .358 with a 1.194 OPS, 15 homers and 70 RBI, and 46 walks against 25 strikeouts. He was a second-team NAIA All-American and is on the 2027 roster.

label: Scoring
detail: Indiana Tech scored 9.10 runs a game in NAIA stats, 1st of 11 in the WHAC and 13th of 179 in the NAIA. It hit .314, 4th in the WHAC.

label: Speed
detail: 144 steals in 167 tries was 2.40 a game, 4th in the WHAC. Santana had 27, Ruiz and Dunkle 21 each, McEldowney 15 and Morrison 14. Pudlik had 12 with 9 at-bats.

label: Getting on base
detail: The .441 on-base percentage ranked 2nd in the WHAC, with 13.5% of plate appearances ending in a walk and 128 hit by pitches. Santana reached at a .513 clip with 47 walks and 19 hit by pitches.

label: League play
detail: Indiana Tech went 24-4 in the WHAC and outscored those opponents 315-98, hitting .352 with a 3.41 ERA in those 28 games. It went 12-9 outside the WHAC in the regular season. Two of the four WHAC losses were at Northwestern Ohio, by 1 and 3 runs.

label: Against ranked teams
detail: It beat No. 6 Cumberlands three times, No. 2 Georgia Gwinnett once in two tries, No. 4 Tennessee Wesleyan once in two tries and No. 17 Abraham Baldwin once, and lost twice to No. 1 Taylor. Ranks are as printed on Indiana Tech's schedule page.

label: Late innings
detail: Leatherman had 11 of the 16 saves and is a grad student who isn't on the 2027 roster. May had 2, and Baughman, VanOeveren and Sommer 1 each.

label: Catcher
detail: Ferguson made 51 starts at catcher and 6 at DH and is listed as INF/C for 2027. Roberson made 4 and is a listed senior. Lukasik, Negron, Farris and Manning, who has no 2026 stats, are back, and the 2027 roster adds Auker, Beggs, Goodwin and Lutz at catcher.

label: First base
detail: Morrison made 48 starts and is a listed senior. Seefeldt made 12 and is back. The 2027 roster adds Gomez at first.

label: Middle infield
detail: Dunkle made 59 starts at short and is back. At second, McEldowney made 34, Ruiz 18 and Morrison 8, and none of them is on the 2027 roster.

label: Third base
detail: Hannah made 56 starts and is back, with 13 homers. Hammond made 4.

label: Outfield
detail: Rainey made 58 starts in center and Richards 44 in right, and both are back. Santana made 41 in left and 10 in right and is a listed senior. Roberson made 15 in left and is also a listed senior. Laymon is back after 8 starts.

label: Designated hitter
detail: Ruiz made 37 starts here and isn't on the 2027 roster. Hammond made 9 and Ferguson 6.

label: Rotation
detail: Redmon (15), Myers (11) and Byford (9) made 35 of the 60 starts and aren't on the 2027 roster. Hammond (8), Baughman (7), VanOeveren (5), Plank (3) and Keegan Miller (2) are back.

label: Bullpen
detail: Leatherman (23 relief outings), May (17), Sommer (15), Robinson (14) and Glaser (13) aren't on the 2027 roster. Plank (16) is back and made the most relief outings of anyone who returns.

label: On the 2027 roster
detail: 22 players from the 2026 roster, including Ferguson, Rainey, Hannah, Dunkle, Richards, Hammond, Baughman and Plank.

label: Listed senior hitters not on it, 10 or more at-bats
detail: Ben Morrison, Jorge Santana, Noah McEldowney, Jacoby Roberson, Logan Rybarczyk.

label: Other hitters not on it, 10 or more at-bats
detail: Derek Ruiz. Ruiz was a listed junior and a first-team All-WHAC DH in 2026. His next stop isn't confirmed here.

label: Pitchers not on it, 10 or more innings
detail: Noah Redmon (72.1 IP), Luke Myers (42.1 IP), Danny May (36.1 IP), Austin Byford (34.2 IP), Colton Leatherman (29.2 IP), Dean Sommer (26.2 IP), Kade Robinson (21.0 IP), Gary Glaser III (13.0 IP). Redmon, first-team All-WHAC, and Byford, a Gold Glove pick, were listed sophomores in 2026. Their next stops aren't confirmed here.

label: New names on the 2027 roster
detail: 46 players not on the 2026 roster page, listed on the Recruiting tab. 26 are listed as freshmen or redshirt freshmen. 12 list Fort Wayne as a hometown.

label: Kip McWilliams, head coach
detail: His bio lists 665-396-2 entering 2025-26, his 20th season, and 2026 adds 43-17 for 708-413-2. It also lists seven WHAC Tournament titles, four WHAC regular-season titles, 15 trips to the NAIA National Championship and one Avista NAIA World Series, and WHAC Coach of the Year in 2012, 2018 and 2019.

label: Brent Alwine, associate head coach
detail: His bio says he handles most of the recruiting and works with infielders and hitters, and that he was an associate scout for the Texas Rangers from 2013 to 2018 and director of Prep Baseball Report Michigan in 2013 and 2014.

label: Gordon Turner, assistant coach
detail: His bio, written for 2024-25, lists his 17th year as an assistant. It says he coaches outfielders and helps with hitters, and that he played at Indiana Tech in 2009.

label: Hayden Jones, assistant coach
detail: His bio says he joined for 2024-25 as hitting and catching coach, after signing with the Cincinnati Reds in 2021 and playing in the minor leagues.

label: Justin Huff, Luke Huerta and Craig Grow, assistant coaches
detail: Listed on the staff page. Their bios have no details. A Luke Huerta played for Indiana Tech in 2025.

label: Where the roster comes from
detail: 22 of 49 list an Indiana hometown and 11 a Michigan one. 4 list Ohio and 3 Illinois. Two list Puerto Rico, and one each lists Ontario, Panama and South Australia.

label: How players arrive
detail: 29 of 49 list no college before Indiana Tech, 13 a two-year college and 7 a four-year school. The roster lists only one previous school per player.

label: Transfers on the field
detail: Ruiz came from Lander, Richards from Macomb CC, McEldowney from Wright State-Lake, Baughman from Calumet, VanOeveren from Kankakee, May from Lassen, Leatherman from Grand Rapids CC and Sommer from Northwestern Ohio. Macomb CC sent five players to the 2026 roster, the most of any school.

label: Rochester Christian is missing from NAIA stats
detail: The NAIA stats team table lists 11 WHAC teams, without Rochester Christian. Indiana Tech's WHAC ranks are out of those 11, while Cleary's column on this page was worked out earlier against 12. Side-by-side edges compare the two teams' actual numbers.

label: Official conference lines include two extra games
detail: The conference tables on Indiana Tech's stats page show 25-5 and 330-113 over 30 games. Its schedule page shows 24-4, and McWilliams's bio agrees. The two extra games are tournament games, the Apr 30 loss to Lawrence Tech and the May 3 win over Madonna, and removing them gives 315-98 exactly. Every WHAC line here is added up from the 28 regular-season box scores, so they won't match that table.

label: Hitting gaps against published stats
detail: Season lines here are the official ones; filters add up the box scores. Official then box score: Hannah runs 45, 46. Keegan Miller runs 5, 4. Keegan Miller's games played are 18 officially and 17 in box scores. At-bats, hits, walks, strikeouts and RBI tie for every hitter.

label: Pitching gaps against published stats
detail: Official then box score: May hits 46, 47. Wild pitches: Redmon 4, 3, and Robinson 5, 4. NAIA stats shows 504 hits allowed to the official 503. Errors are 67 officially and 66 in the line scores. Opponent steals are 65-85 officially and 66-86 in play-by-play. Everything else ties.

label: One decision worked out by elimination
detail: The Mar 25 box score at Marian lists no decision. Hammond started that game, and he's the only pitcher one loss short of his published line (6-2), so the outing log gives him that loss. No recap was checked for it.

label: Forfeit labels ignored
detail: NAIA stats labels both Mar 15 games at Rochester Christian as forfeits because Rochester Christian had an ineligible player. They're recorded here as played, 7-5 and 20-4, the same way Indiana Tech's schedule and stats count them.

label: Some games have no real counts
detail: 9 of the 60 box scores have no usable counts: 7 list none, the May 2 Cleary game lists every count as 0-0, and the May 1 Cornerstone game has counts on only 9 of 100 plate appearances. Those games are left out of the count and pitch stats. Counts appear for about 85% of plate appearances.

label: Roster gaps and typos
detail: Bats and throws are blank for Pudlik and McEldowney, so pull and opposite-field shares are blank for them. Medina's height is blank and his previous school repeats his high school, so I left it off. On the 2027 page I read "Elhart" as Elkhart, "Bayamen" as Bayamon and "Kankaee Valley" as Kankakee Valley.

label: Player names differ by source
detail: Box scores call VanOeveren Andrew, and many scorers spell him VanOevern. The roster and season stats say Drew VanOeveren, and that's what this page uses. Keegan and Kaiden Miller share an initial, so plays use "Ke. Miller."

label: 2027 roster is a posted page, not a final one
detail: It lists 68 players, and the projections here use it as posted. Being off it doesn't confirm where a player went. New names means not on the 2026 roster page, not necessarily new to the school: Berkey, Bohde, Ryan Hammond, Hodges, Long, Mobley and Santiago are on it and were listed with Indiana Tech by the WHAC in 2026, so they aren't new to the school.

label: Coach record
detail: McWilliams's bio says 665-396-2 entering 2025-26. Adding 43-17 from the 2026 schedule gives 708-413-2, which is what this page uses. I didn't add up all 20 seasons.

label: Projections
detail: Projected lineups and staffs come from public numbers and the posted roster. Indiana Tech has published no depth chart. New names have no 2026 stats here, so none is in a projected spot.

label: Map sources
detail: Hometowns are from Indiana Tech's roster. I entered coordinates by hand, so towns are approximate. Ledgard (South Australia) and Santana (Panama) are off the map's edges and aren't plotted. Medina lists only Puerto Rico, so he's placed mid-island. Shapes come from U.S. Census and Natural Earth.

label: Games that were not played
detail: NAIA stats lists a Mar 18 game with IU Kokomo as postponed, and Indiana Tech's schedule lists an Apr 15 doubleheader at St. Francis (Ill.) as canceled. None is counted.

label: Commits
detail: No commit list for Indiana Tech was found. The Recruiting tab lists the new names on its 2027 roster instead.

label: Checked by arithmetic
detail: The game log adds to 43-17, 546 runs scored and 327 allowed, and to 24-4 in WHAC games. Line scores match those run totals. Home, away and neutral records match the schedule page. The play log's 2,465 plate appearances and 2,187 batters faced match the official totals.

label: WHAC site
detail: Honors, the tournament results and the final standings come from whac.net. The WHAC's list counts 10 All-WHAC Warriors, which matches McWilliams's bio.

label: Vs Cleary starts at 2019
detail: The series is from Indiana Tech's schedule pages for 2019 through 2026, because its opponent history page didn't open. 2020's two games were canceled. Both Apr 19, 2021 games show as 14-4 on that page, which I kept as written.

label: Box scores are from NAIA stats
detail: Indiana Tech's site uses a different stats system, so game data comes from NAIA stats. All 60 games are there.

label: Starts in the hitter table
detail: The official batting table carries pitching starts. Hammond shows 21 starts there, and the lineup and usage tables show 15, because they count batting-order starts from box scores. Keegan Miller shows 2 and 0.

label: Spray charts are partial
detail: Spray charts use 1,460 of Indiana Tech's 1,924 at-bats (76%): 96% of balls in play, 90% of hits (543 of 605) and 99% of everything else (917 of 922). Strikeouts have no direction. Scorers skip the direction on hits far more often than on outs, so charts can understate hits. Zones are where the scorer placed the ball, not exact spots.

label: Direction corrected
detail: Double plays were being credited to the relay throw instead of the first fielder, and plays written with the last name first or an error by a fielder had no direction. I corrected that, which moved Pull, Center and Oppo a few points for some hitters and raised the direction counts.

label: Runs by inning
detail: Indiana Tech scored most in the 5th (97 runs), then the 6th (81), and 76 in the 1st. It scored 98 from the 7th on, though 7-inning games shorten that count.

label: Runs allowed
detail: Opponents scored most in the 5th, 49 runs, and 36 in the 1st.

label: Steals
detail: Play-by-play shows 111 steals of second, 21 of third and 12 of home, all 144 published. It shows Indiana Tech caught 23 times, which matches the official line.

label: Where Indiana Tech has the edge
detail: On-base percentage .441 to .433, slugging .460 to .453, OPS .901 to .886, wOBA .401 to .393, runs per game 9.10 to 7.69, homers per game 0.85 to 0.40, steals per game 2.40 to 1.44, walk rate 13.5% to 13.4%, ERA 5.33 to 5.70, FIP 6.05 to 6.11, WHIP 1.52 to 1.58, walks plus hit batters per nine 5.40 to 7.29.

label: Where Cleary has the edge
detail: Batting average .320 to .314, strikeout rate 14.1% to 16.1%, strikeouts per nine 8.53 to 8.08, homers allowed per nine 0.56 to 0.88, fielding percentage .968 to .967.

label: Series
detail: Indiana Tech won all 3 meetings in 2026, two on Mar 21 and one in the WHAC Tournament. Since 2019 it leads 16-1. Cleary's one win was 6-5 on Apr 29, 2023.

label: Mar 21: Indiana Tech 5, Cleary 3
detail: Redmon started for Indiana Tech (6.1 IP, 2 ER) and Parris for Cleary (5.0 IP, 4 ER). Hammond went 2-for-3 for Indiana Tech, and Kempainen went 1-for-2 for Cleary.

label: Mar 21: Indiana Tech 14, Cleary 5
detail: Baughman started for Indiana Tech (3.0 IP, 2 ER) and Noseworthy for Cleary (1.0 IP, 0 ER). Ferguson went 2-for-5 for Indiana Tech, and Wesley went 2-for-4 for Cleary.

label: May 2, WHAC Tournament: Indiana Tech 13, Cleary 2
detail: VanOeveren started for Indiana Tech (8.0 IP, 2 ER) and Fay for Cleary (7.0 IP, 4 ER). Santana went 3-for-4 for Indiana Tech, and Mackay went 2-for-3 for Cleary.

label: Method
detail: With All games selected, every number in this view counts all 60 games, from box scores and play-by-play. Ground outs include sacrifices and fielder's choices, and air outs include sacrifice flies.

label: Partial
detail: Scorers didn't enter these details for every game, so each number covers only part of the season. Treat them as samples. The first two tables show what's missing.

label: Splits
detail: Innings and time through the order use every plate appearance. Time through the order is each pitcher's batters faced in that game divided by nine, so substitutions can shift it slightly.

label: Splits
detail: Only plate appearances with a count listed. The count is where the plate appearance stood before its final pitch. Two strikes and Full count overlap the other rows.

label: Ground and air outs
detail: McEldowney has 2.14 ground outs per air out, the most among regulars (100 or more plate appearances), and Ferguson has 0.51.

label: How long arms go
detail: Baughman averages 5.1 innings a start, Redmon 4.8 and Hammond 4.6. Plank goes 2.9 per relief outing and May 2.1.

label: Groundball and fly-ball arms
detail: Baughman has 1.57 ground outs per air out, the most among pitchers with 100 batters faced, and Sommer has 0.49.

label: First-pitch swings
detail: Among regulars with pitch data on 60 or more plate appearances, Ferguson swings at the most first pitches, 28% on 213. Santana swings at the fewest, 8% on 213.

label: Swing and miss
detail: Morrison whiffs on 12% of swings, the fewest among regulars with pitch data on 60 or more plate appearances, and Hannah and Richards on 23%. On the mound, Byford gets a whiff on 28% of swings and Baughman on 19%, among pitchers with pitch data on 100 or more batters.

label: Direction
detail: Richards pulls 54% of his batted balls, the most among regulars, on 108 with a direction. Morrison pulls 32%, on 155. McEldowney has no listed batting side, so Pull and Oppo stay blank for him.

label: Pitch counts
detail: Redmon averages 80 pitches a start and Baughman 72. Redmon's most was 109. Averages use only outings with a listed count.
